title: outstandR's G-computation estimate moved by about 0.05 on the log odds ratio across defensible target reconstructions
question: How much does outstandR's G-computation estimate depend on how it reconstructs the aggregate trial's covariate distribution from published means and SDs, when the true covariates are skewed and tail-dependent?
design: Skewed target covariates with a Clayton or Gaussian copula, IPD with the same or a different correlation; outstandR's G-computation under five reconstructions (default, reported correlation, independence, gamma margins); anchored binary-outcome comparison. 4 cells, 400 replicates each.
answer: Partly. Across five defensible reconstructions of the aggregate trial's covariates (normal or gamma margins; the IPD's, the target's, or no correlation), outstandR's G-computation estimate ranged by 0.049 to 0.052 on the log odds ratio scale within a dataset: at the registered materiality threshold, but about a fifth of its sampling SD. The default (normal margins, IPD correlation) was biased by -0.02 to -0.06 on skewed covariates; gamma margins removed most of it. Tail dependence in the true copula changed the range by at most 0.002.
findings: Margin family and correlation choice each contributed about half of the range.
Independence was the worst reconstruction; the IPD's correlation added bias when the target's differed.
Registered verdict: material, with the range at the threshold in every cell.
not_answered: Pairwise anchored comparison, two covariates, correct outcome model, point estimates only; no Bayesian G-computation, multiple-imputation marginalization or network use. Peer review has not been done.
estimand: Anchored marginal log odds ratio B versus A in the target
methods_compared: outstandR G-computation under five covariate reconstructions
